title: Review: pH and Kw; Strong and weak acids
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB02#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB03#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB03#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB02#N.4, AB03#N.4a, AB02#N.12, AB03#N.11, AB02#N.10a, AB03#N.3a, AB02#N.6, AB03#N.7. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutral solution
items.clue: An aqueous mixture in which [H⁺] equals [OH⁻].

items.label: Concentration
items.clue: The amount of a dissolved substance per unit volume.

items.label: Strong acid
items.clue: Dissociates effectively completely in water, as HNO₃ does.

items.label: Universal indicator
items.clue: Paper or liquid matched against a chart to estimate pH to about 1 unit.

questions.stem: Hydrobromic acid, HBr, is a strong acid. What is the pH of 4.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ HBr(aq)?
questions.explanation: HBr ionises completely, so [H⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻³ and pH = −log₁₀(4.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.40.

questions.stem: Solution X is 0.0010 mol dm⁻³ KOH(aq). Solution Y is 2.0 mol dm⁻³ NH₃(aq). Which statement is correct?

options.text: NH₃ is the stronger base, as solution Y is more concentrated.
NH₃ is not a base, as its formula contains no OH group.
KOH is the stronger base, as it is fully dissociated.
Both are strong bases, as both release OH⁻ ions in water.

questions.explanation: Strength is the extent of dissociation, not concentration. KOH is fully dissociated even when dilute; NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ lies well to the left.

questions.stem: Two samples of rain are tested with a pH meter. Sample A has pH 4.2; sample B has pH 5.7. How does [H⁺] in sample A compare with [H⁺] in sample B?

options.text: It is 1.5 times greater, as the pH values differ by 1.5.
It is about 15 times greater: 10 times for each pH unit.
It is about 32 times greater.
It is about 32 times smaller, as sample A has the lower pH.

questions.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ, so the ratio is 10⁻⁴·² ÷ 10⁻⁵·⁷ = 10¹·⁵ ≈ 32. Lower pH, more H⁺.

questions.stem: Which statement about solutions P and Q is correct? P is 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq). Q is 0.50 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COOH(aq), measured pH 2.53.

options.text: P has the lower pH, as a strong acid always has a lower pH than a weak one.
P has the higher pH, even though HCl is the stronger acid.
CH₃COOH must be a strong acid, as Q has a lower pH than P.
HCl is a weak acid in P, as its concentration is low.

questions.explanation: P: pH = −log₁₀(5.0 × 10⁻⁴) = 3.30. Only about 1 in 170 CH₃COOH molecules in Q dissociates, but Q is 1000 times more concentrated, so [H⁺] ≈ 2.95 × 10⁻³, pH 2.53. pH depends on concentration as well as strength.

questions.stem: At 298 K, solution P has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ and solution Q has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Kw = 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶. How does [OH⁻] in P compare with [OH⁻] in Q?

options.text: It is 100 times larger in P than in Q.
It is the same, as acid has no effect on [OH⁻].
Neither contains OH⁻ ions, as both are acidic.
It is 100 times smaller in P than in Q.

questions.explanation: [OH⁻] = Kw/[H⁺]: P 1.0 × 10⁻¹¹, Q 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³. P has 100 times the [H⁺], so 1/100 of the [OH⁻].

questions.stem: A solution of nitric acid, HNO₃(aq), has a concentration of 0.0010 mol dm⁻³. Which statement about this solution is correct?

options.text: It is a weak acid, as its concentration is low.
It contains mainly HNO₃ molecules with a few ions.
It is a dilute solution of an acid that is fully dissociated.
It is neutral, as this much water neutralises the acid.

questions.explanation: HNO₃ → H⁺ + NO₃⁻ completely, so [H⁺] = 0.0010 mol dm⁻³. Strength and concentration are independent.

questions.stem: A student needs the pH of a solution. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Universal indicator gives the pH to two decimal places if the colour is matched carefully.
A pH meter calibrated with buffers of known pH gives a reading to about 0.01 unit.
A pH meter needs no calibration, as its reading is electronic.
Universal indicator is a single indicator that changes colour only at pH 7.

questions.explanation: Calibrated against buffers, a pH meter gives a precise numerical reading, usually to 0.01. Universal indicator only estimates pH.

questions.stem: Methanoic acid is a weak acid: HCOOH(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ HCOO⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq). Which statement is correct?

options.text: The equilibrium lies to the right, as all acids dissociate in water.
The equilibrium lies to the left, as HCOO⁻ is a weaker base than H₂O.
The equilibrium lies to the right, as HCOO⁻ is the weaker of the two bases.
The equilibrium lies to the left, as H₃O⁺ is a stronger acid than HCOOH.

questions.explanation: Equilibrium favours the weaker acid and weaker base. HCOOH is weaker than H₃O⁺, and H₂O weaker than HCOO⁻, so the left is favoured: few molecules dissociate.
